name: Crown imperial
grown_as: A tall garden bulb. William's is 'William Rex', with deep orange-red bells flushed and veined darker. ⚠️ CHECK the colour; other varieties are orange or yellow.
habit: A single stout, upright stem 70 to 100 cm tall, leafy in its lower half, bare in the middle and topped with a ring of hanging bells under a tuft of green leaves. The whole plant has a strong foxy smell.

leaf.arrangement: Many leaves in crowded whorls of three or four (or scattered) round the lower half of the stem; above the flowers a crown of 10 to 20 smaller leaf-like bracts
leaf.outline: Lance-shaped, 10 to 20 cm long by 2 to 4 cm wide
leaf.base: Stalkless, joined straight to the stem
leaf.veins: Several parallel veins running the length

flower.form: Large hanging bells in a ring, under a topknot of leaves like a pineapple
flower.petals: Six tepals, free, oblong, forming a broad bell
flower.centre: Inside, at the base of each tepal, a large white nectary holding a drop of nectar; yellow anthers and the style hang just below the rim
flower.behind: No sepals; above the ring of bells the crown of green leafy bracts
flower.carried: Three to eight bells hanging in a single ring (umbel) at the top of the stem, all facing down, with the leafy crown standing above them

fruit: The capsules turn to stand upright under the leafy crown: six-winged (six-ridged), about 3 to 4 cm, green ripening to brown and splitting to release flat brown seeds.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from bought bulbs.
winter: Nothing above ground until the fat shoots appear in February or March.

bloom: a broad hanging bell of six tepals, orange-red with darker veins
white nectaries with drops showing inside the base
anthers and style just below the rim
bulb: a very large round bulb 8 to 12 cm of fleshy cream-yellow scales
a hole down the centre where last year's stem was
shoots: a thick fleshy shoot like a giant asparagus spear, often flushed purple
flower: a tall stout stem, leafy in the lower half and bare above
a ring of hanging orange-red bells at the top
a tuft of green leaves standing above the bells
seedhead: upright winged pods in a ring under the leafy crown
the leafy crown and leafy lower stem still green
dormant: the stem dying yellow and brown, or nothing above the soil

look_alikes: Fritillaria persica has a spike of small dark purple bells and no leafy crown. Fritillaria raddeana is smaller with pale yellow bells. The young shoot can be mistaken for a lily, but lily leaves run the whole length of the stem.
